title: My face right now would fit in this show quite well  #theoutsiders #n...
transcript: I recently went to Lahoya Playhouse in California to see The Outsiders musical, which is a world premiere musical based off the novel and film of the same name. I thought I knew the story going in, and it turns out I was getting mixed up with the Warriors, which is a very different narrative. And it turns out I don't know this story at all. Now, this is a world premier musical, so I expected to see a show that was very much still in development. And not only was it a world premier musical, but I saw the second ever performance of it. And it was so in development that Christopher Ashley, who's the artistic director of Loya Playhouse and also the director of Diana the musical, came out before the show started to say, hey, uh, welcome to our show. We literally added a song today, and the intermission is going to take a little longer than expected cause we're working out the transition. So already I was like, all right, this is gonna be a work in progress. And it was very much a work in progress. Some of the creator team, including the choreographers, were sitting right behind me taking notes the whole show. There were definitely technical difficulties. The sound was a little wonky at the start of the show, and even just some of the blocking, you could tell that they were still getting used to it. Like it wasn't fully settled in. Yet. And I think the show still has a lot of work to do. But that being said, there's a lot of promising stuff in the show. I really loved the sound of the score. I wasn't a huge fan of all of the songs, but I think it has a really interesting sound that lends itself to the story pretty well. And there are some stunning visuals in this. There's a lot of, uh, cars and trains in the show, and the way that they do those is pretty gorgeous. There's a lot of fight sequences in the show, and they try different styles with them. Whenever they tried to do a more realistic style, it didn't really work for me. But there's some very theatrical fighting in this that I thought was just stunning. And a very clever way to put fighting in a musical. Overall, I didn't love the show. This wasn't a story I was familiar with. And I kind of wanna go and watch the movie or read the book, because I feel like it took me a little too long to understand what the narrative was going for. That being said, though, there's a lot in here that I genuinely enjoyed. And I'm very curious to see how this story turns out down the road after they keep working on it a little more. And if you end up going to see it later on the run, let me know what you think, because This definitely is one that you can tell they are working on a lot in this preview period.
classificationReason: Creator attended The Outsiders musical at La Jolla Playhouse (second performance) and shares detailed opinions about the production, development process, and technical aspects
